Physiotherapy (also called physical therapy) is a health care profession that assesses, diagnoses, treats and works to prevent physical impairments, pain, movement limitations and disability caused by injury, illness, ageing or congenital conditions. It uses evidence-based physical approaches—such as therapeutic exercise, manual therapy, electrotherapy, education, and functional training—to restore or improve mobility, strength, endurance, balance, coordination and overall physical function. 

Key elements:
- Goals: reduce pain, restore movement and function, prevent deterioration or recurrence, promote independence and participation in daily life.  
- Methods: exercise prescription, hands-on techniques (mobilization/manipulation), soft-tissue work, postural education, gait training, assistive device provision, ergonomic advice, and modalities like ultrasound, TENS or heat/ice when appropriate.  
- Settings: hospitals, outpatient clinics, community health, rehabilitation centers, sports and occupational settings, schools and home care.  
- Providers: regulated professionals (physiotherapists/physical therapists) who work collaboratively with patients and other healthcare team members.
